statements.statement: An in-memory cache stores data on disk for long-term persistence.
statements.explanation: An in-memory cache stores data in RAM, not on disk, which makes it fast but volatile. Data is lost when the system restarts.

statements.statement: In-memory caches are ideal for storing frequently accessed data to improve application performance.
statements.explanation: By storing frequently accessed data in RAM, applications can retrieve it quickly, significantly improving performance compared to accessing data from disk.

statements.statement: Data stored in an in-memory cache is retained even after a system reboot.
statements.explanation: In-memory caches are volatile, meaning data is lost when the system is restarted or crashes, unlike persistent storage solutions.

statements.statement: In-memory caches should not be used for critical data that cannot be lost.
statements.explanation: Due to their volatile nature, in-memory caches are best suited for transient data that can be regenerated or fetched again, not for storing critical data that needs to be persistent.
